title: Alex's Morning Brief
vibe: Sample data. Every company and link here is made up so you can see the layout. Agents had a big morning, pricing got weird, and Austin got a new meetup.
tldr: A (fictional) agent platform cut prices in half and moved to usage billing.
A survey from a (fictional) research firm says most teams still run agents in pilot only.
Austin's newest AI meetup opens its doors next Thursday.

stories.spark: Half-price agents: the usage-billing boss fight begins
stories.summary: Example Labs cut the price of its agent platform by 50% and switched from seats to pay-per-task billing. Existing customers move over next quarter. The company says small teams were the reason.
stories.why_it_matters: You own pricing. If buyers start expecting per-task pricing for agents, your seat-based plan will get compared against it in every deal.
stories.angle: Expect two or three rivals to copy this within a month.

stories.spark: Agents in production? Most teams are still in the tutorial level
stories.summary: A survey of 400 companies by Sample Research found that 6 in 10 are testing AI agents, but fewer than 1 in 5 run one in production. Cost and reliability were the top blockers.
stories.why_it_matters: Useful ammo for your build decision: the market is early, so a reliable, narrow agent could stand out more than a broad one.

stories.spark: A free model that fits on a laptop just dropped
stories.summary: The Demo Collective released an open-weight model small enough to run on a recent laptop. Early testers on forums say it handles short coding tasks well. Independent benchmarks are not out yet.
stories.why_it_matters: If small local models keep improving, your team could prototype agent features without paying per call.

stories.spark: Austin gets a new AI builders night, and it's free
stories.summary: A new monthly meetup for people building with AI starts next Thursday downtown. The first session is a show-and-tell with five short demos.
stories.why_it_matters: You said you want to meet people building nearby. This is the easiest first step.

move.title: Price-check yourself
move.detail: Spend 10 minutes writing what your product would cost per task instead of per seat. You'll want that number before a customer asks.

talking_points: Agent pricing is sliding from seats to tasks, so we should know our per-task cost.
Most companies are still piloting agents, so reliability is the real differentiator.

quick_hits.text: A (fictional) note-taking app added an AI meeting recap feature.
Sample Cloud raised prices on its smallest plan by $2 a month.

items.text: A (fictional) robotics startup is hiring 30 engineers for its new office.
